reconciliation.statement: Every instance is claimed by AT MOST ONE row: matching runs ENFORCED → NAMED → GENERAL and stops at the first hit, so a named row's instances are removed from its general row rather than added on top. generalRowTotal + namedRowTotal + intraPackageExcluded + matchedNoRow must equal rawInstances. Cells collapsed for being empty held zero instances by construction (that is the collapse condition), so the collapse cannot move any count — they are listed by name in `summary.collapsedCells`.

rules.rule: founder Ruling 1(3) — API / MCP / events are the legal cross-Layer mechanisms. BINDING. SPECIFIED ONLY — no lint enforces it. Emitting and subscribing are the same crossing with the same counterparty: the bus. `EventBus` is ANONYMOUS pub/sub — an emitter names an event TYPE, never a package — so there is no such thing as sending an event "to" a Layer or a Service. Attributing a crossing to whichever package happens to hold a subscriber manufactures rules that do not exist; the emitter→subscriber graph is reported as evidence in `summary.events`, not as rows.

END STATE: a framework package is not an EventBus endpoint. `shared` is the leaf everybody imports, not a participant with behaviour. One production instance — `framework/shared/src/observability/dispatcher.ts:473`, `bus.on("*", …)` — and the DESIGN is good (one wildcard subscription instead of wiring 30+ call sites, with an exhaustiveness check that turns a new event into a compile error). Keep the subscriber; move it out of `shared` into a module allowed to be an endpoint. Ruling 12.3 lists that relocation as a follow-up work package, so this is warned now and enforced when it lands — the rule states the end state either way. While it sits in `shared`, every emit in the repo resolves to a framework subscriber, which is why the old subscriber-attributed rows tracked total emit volume.
